title: How Much Does the End of One Word Overlap the Start of the Other?

concept.title: The prefix function of b + a separator + a, read at its last position, is the longest suffix of a that is a prefix of b
body: Two words `a` and `b` are given. When the word `b` is glued after `a`, their ends can overlap: the last letters of `a` may be the same as the first letters of `b`. Find the **longest overlap**, that is, the length of the longest word that is a **suffix of `a`** and a **prefix of `b`**. For `a = abcab` and `b = cabxyz` the overlap is `cab` (3), so `a` and `b` can be glued as `abcabxyz`. For `a = abc` and `b = abc` it is 3, for `a = abc` and `b = xyz` it is 0.

Write one word `c = b + "#" + a`, with a separator `#` that is not a letter. In the prefix function of `c`, the value at the last position is the length of the longest proper prefix of `c` that is also a suffix of `c`. A prefix of `c` that is also a suffix cannot contain the separator (the suffix part lies after it), so it is a prefix of `b` that is also a suffix of `a`: exactly the overlap. The separator also prevents the value from exceeding `|b|`.

body.code:
c = b + "#" + a
pi = prefix_function(c)
print(pi[-1])                   # the longest suffix of a that is a prefix of b

body: The time is O(|a| + |b|). The overlap is the key quantity in gluing words together, for example when building the shortest word that contains both of them (the next problems use this).

statement: Two words `a` and `b` are given. Print the length of the longest word that is both a suffix of `a` and a prefix of `b` (0 if there is none).
inputFormat: The first line has the word `a`.
The second line has the word `b`.
outputFormat: Print the length of the overlap.
constraints: 1 <= length of a, length of b <= 40000
Both words consist of lowercase English letters.
hints: Glue the words as b + "#" + a.
Compute the prefix function of the glued word.
The last value is the longest suffix of a that is a prefix of b.

explanation: The prefix function of b + "#" + a at its last position is the length of the longest prefix of b that is a suffix of a.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

def prefix_function(s):
    n = len(s)
    pi = [0] * n
    for i in range(1, n):
        k = pi[i - 1]
        while k and s[i] != s[k]:
            k = pi[k - 1]
        if s[i] == s[k]:
            k += 1
        pi[i] = k
    return pi

a = input().strip()
b = input().strip()

c = b + "#" + a
pi = prefix_function(c)
print(pi[-1])
